findings.issue: The artwork JSON download serializes the private record directly, bypassing exportRecordCollection and exporting cloudDeleteUrl capabilities and share URL tokens.
The export sanitizer only cleans cloudShareUrl, leaving credentials in image, thumbnail and imageUrl; URL userinfo and signed URL query parameters also survive.
JPEG fill bytes are skipped in pairs, swallowing an APP11 marker prefix and misclassifying credential-bearing JPEGs as absent. The Worker and Python scanners have the same defect.
Gallery writes persist client-supplied outputSha256 and credentialStatus without comparing them with the uploaded bytes, allowing false provenance on public share pages.

Credential-bearing PNG chunks with corrupt CRCs are reported as present_untrusted, and marker-only detection is labeled structurally valid without validating manifest structure. The browser and Python twins share this behavior.
The production workflow directly invokes Wrangler without the new production-config guard, so PREVIEW_READ_ONLY=true can reach production despite local deploy rejection.

needs-human: Issue #18 requires valid/invalid credential verification and real credential, stripped-image and product roundtrip fixtures. The implementation only detects markers and has no trust-chain validator or real signed-fixture runtime evidence; choosing a verifier/trust policy or narrowing acceptance requires a maintainer decision.

summary: Fixed six review findings covering artwork export capability leaks, signed image URL leaks, JPEG fill-byte parsing, PNG CRC checks and misleading labels, unvalidated gallery claims, and the production config guard bypass; each fix has a regression test proven red before implementation. The full offline gate passed with 602 tests, 26 subtests and three mocked browser QA suites; fixes are committed locally without pushing. needs-human: full C2PA verification, its verifier/trust policy, and real signed-fixture runtime acceptance required by #18 remain unresolved, so fixed is false for the review as a whole.
